query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A machine-learning-based multi-objective optimization method will expedite identification of low-weight, intrinsically strong, and ductile refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) compositions by efficiently exploring the large multi-principal element space.
generation.material_initial_state: Generic refractory high-entropy alloy with multiple refractory elements (e.g., Nb, Mo, Ta, W) in nonequimolar proportions.
generation.intervention: Apply a data-driven, multi-objective optimization approach leveraging existing experimental data and high-throughput calculations to systematically screen candidate compositions for strength, ductility, and low density.
generation.conditions: Use high-performance computing to train and apply the ML model over composition ranges consistent with targeted mechanical and density requirements; verify predictions through measurements of single-phase or multiphase BCC-based RHEAs over a relevant temperature range.
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructural evolution in bcc-based refractory alloys and coherent precipitates, as predicted by computational methods (e.g. CALPHAD) and ML-driven screening.
generation.mechanism: The model correlates composition–property relationships and predicts phase stability, facilitating the tuning of constituent elements for enhanced lattice distortion, projected improved dislocation motion, and controlled formation of strengthening phases.
generation.predicted_outcome: Faster discovery of RHEAs exhibiting higher tensile strength, improved ductility, and reduced density compared to conventional methods, thereby improving trade-offs among these properties.
generation.baseline: Traditional trial-and-error or purely thermo-kinetic-based design strategies that require extensive experimentation and do not easily address multi-objective property targets.
generation.boundary: Limited by the training data availability and model extrapolation capabilities; designed compositions still require experimental validation to confirm predicted performance.
generation.uncertainty: Further high-quality data are required to refine model predictions. The accuracy of mechanical property predictions declines outside the bounds of the training set, introducing uncertainty for novel compositions.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a set of RHEA compositions suggested by the ML-based design framework for improved strength, ductility, and low density. Synthesize lab-scale specimens and conduct mechanical tests (tensile, hardness, and impact) under conditions spanning room to elevated temperatures. Compare measured properties to predicted values.
measurements: Phase stability via X-ray diffraction and microstructural examination
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If, across tested compositions, none shows improved strength-ductility balance with reduced density relative to baseline RHEAs, the hypothesis is disproved. Confirmation of predicted property improvements for at least some ML-recommended compositions supports the hypothesis.

cited_evidence.text: The fields of aerospace and fossil energy have benefited from decades of the development of Ni-base superalloys. However, to obtain further efficiency gains and environmental friendliness, developing new materials with inexpensive, light, and strong characteristics is required. Numerous efforts can be found in the development of novel ferritic superalloys containing a disordered body-centered-cubic (BCC) matrix with ordered B2 and/or L2 1 precipitates due to their good creep resistance at elevated temperatures and relatively lower densities [1] , [2] . However, these emerging precipitation-strengthened ferritic alloys still face some drawbacks, such as the low high-temperature strength and not lightweight, which limit their applications. To overcome these issues, new alloy-design strategies are required. Recently, the concept of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) or multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) has revolutionized the traditional alloy-design strategy, using multi-principal components (≥5) instead of one or two key components [3] – [10] . The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

The computational software could significantly affect the efficiency of HTC since massive calculations are carried out.
